Slay the Nspire 2 — component credits

The port is distributed under GPL-3.0-or-later; see the project LICENSE.
Slay the Spire 2 and its game assets belong to Mega Crit and the respective
owners. Game assets are converted from the player's own installation.

The native runtime uses Igor Pavlov's public-domain LZMA2 decoder (7-Zip
LZMA SDK), from ip7z/7zip commit 9128b80e3a471108678e2b3ec3c985861c8d7b0f.
Unicode-derived character tables are distributed with the
Unicode License V3. Calendar data was collected from .NET culture APIs.
The source uses Ndless platform interfaces and draws on the nZATO port.

The reference arithmetic adapts Go softfloat and math routines.
Copyright 2009–2011 The Go Authors. All rights reserved. See the Go license below. Notices for the logarithm, square root and sine:

Copyright (C) 1993 by Sun Microsystems, Inc. All rights reserved.
Developed at SunPro, a Sun Microsystems, Inc. business.
Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software is freely
granted, provided that this notice is preserved.

Sine coefficients: Cephes Math Library Release 2.8, June 2000.
Copyright 1984, 1987, 1989, 1992, 2000 by Stephen L. Moshier.
May be used freely, without support or guarantee.

Reference implementations: https://go.dev/src/runtime/softfloat64.go and
https://go.dev/src/math/ . These notices do not grant rights in the original
game or imply exact last-bit equivalence to its Windows math library.

Color and particle mathematics: Godot contributors and Björn Ottosson;
see the MIT notice below. Boot glyphs derive from Noto Sans CJK SC.
The converter can also use Noto Emoji and Noto Sans Symbols 2 for
characters missing from a game font. The OFL notice below
identifies the corresponding font authors and redistribution terms.

https://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html
https://www.unicode.org/
https://go.dev/
https://github.com/godotengine/godot
https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk
https://github.com/googlefonts/noto-emoji
https://github.com/notofonts/symbols

Godot and OkHSV
--------------=

Godot 4.5.1 rainbow, OkHSV and particle process mathematics

OkHSV sampling derives from Godot 4.5.1-stable's ok_color.h.
Copyright(c) 2021 Björn Ottosson
Rainbow phase follows Godot Engine rich_text_label.cpp.
Offline Ancient and card-Affliction particle sampling adapts ParticleProcessMaterial from
scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp; its curl construction credits
Isaac Cohen, as acknowledged in the Godot source:

Copyright (c) 2014-present Godot Engine contributors (see AUTHORS.md).
Copyright (c) 2007-2014 Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur.

this software and associated documentation files (the "Software"), to deal in
the Software without restriction, including without limitation the rights to

of the Software, and to permit persons to whom the Software is furnished to do
so, subject to the following conditions:
The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all
copies or substantial portions of the Software.

FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
